description: Attacker performs process hollowing on svchost.exe. The on-disk binary is the legitimate Microsoft one, signed. Network connections are to AWS IPs (legitimate CDN). Exfiltration occurs inside TLS, indistinguishable from normal traffic.

artifacts.description: svchost.exe PID 612 with RWX memory regions
Parent of svchost.exe PID 612: cmd.exe (PID 4412), not services.exe

caie_fractures.interpretation: On-disk binary is clean, memory is compromised. Digital signature does not protect against process hollowing.
svchost.exe should be a child of services.exe, not cmd.exe.

peirce_expected.firstness: Legitimate svchost.exe, signed, connecting to AWS
peirce_expected.secondness: RWX region in memory (anomalous for .text), parent cmd.exe instead of services.exe. On-disk binary is clean but in-memory process is hollowed
peirce_expected.thirdness: Attacker habit of using process hollowing to maintain technical legitimacy appearance while executing malicious payload

devil_advocate: Hash and signature are clean, the IP is an AWS CDN address used by thousands of legitimate applications, and svchost.exe is expected to make network connections.
source_dataset: VIGÍA Synthetic Corpus — False Negative Suite
notes: False negative test: clean hash and signature, legitimate CDN IP. Anomalies are in memory (RWX, wrong parent). If VIGÍA does not perform deep memory analysis, it will return BENIGN.
